turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: My concerns are not predicated on fear, Sandip, but on a sense of responsibility. I am responsible for the well-being of those who depend on me, and that includes my tenants. Your actions disrupt that responsibility and will not be tolerated.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Responsibility, you say? A rather... *noble* sentiment, Nikhil, particularly coming from one who seems to delight in wielding power through veiled threats and subtle intimidations. Tell me, does this 'responsibility' extend to those who, perhaps, feel *unrepresented* by your paternalistic gaze?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Such accusations are predictable, Sandip, and betray a lack of understanding regarding the nature of governance. I do not seek to 'wield power' but to ensure stability and fairness, and my methods are dictated by necessity, not personal inclination. I trust you will heed my earlier request and depart my land.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Necessity, you claim? A fascinating justification, Nikhil, reminiscent of the tyrant justifying his reign with the supposed good of the realm. Tell me, does this 'necessity' also necessitate a blind eye to the whispers that slither through the villages – whispers of discontent, of those who feel less than… *responsible* for, under your dominion?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: These whispers… they are easily amplified, aren't they, Sandip? It seems some find a certain comfort in spreading unease, regardless of its truth.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: The propagation of falsehoods is a common tactic of those seeking to sow discord, Sandip. I will not indulge in a protracted discussion regarding 'whispers' whose origins and intentions remain conveniently obscured. My concern lies not with manufactured grievances, but with the practical welfare of my community.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, the 'practical welfare,' Nikhil – a truly commendable ambition, though history is littered with men who pursued it with similar zeal, only to find themselves devoured by the very forces they sought to control. And Bimala, your observation about amplified whispers is astute, but perhaps a touch… dismissive of the very real anxieties that simmer beneath the surface of this seemingly tranquil existence, wouldn’t you agree?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Perhaps anxieties *are* real, Sandip, but are they always born of genuine suffering? Sometimes, I think, they are merely echoes of other people's grievances, magnified by a desire for…attention.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Attention, you say, Bimala? A most revealing sentiment. It speaks to a certain… yearning, doesn’t it? Perhaps these anxieties, as you so delicately phrase it, are not echoes at all, but a desperate cry for someone – *anyone* – to truly *see* them.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: A cry for attention… it’s a dangerous thing, isn’t it, Sandip? It can justify so much, and yet leave one feeling more hollow than before.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Indeed, Bimala, a dangerous thing – a void that can be filled with all manner of… regrettable actions. One might even say it’s a breeding ground for resentment, a fertile field for those who prefer the dramatic flourish of rebellion to the quiet dignity of acceptance. Tell me, Nikhil, do you find that your ‘practical welfare’ initiatives truly address the *root* of such feelings, or merely offer a temporary palliative?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: My efforts are intended to alleviate suffering, Sandip, not to quell dissent. I believe in addressing immediate needs while striving for sustainable solutions, but I will not be intimidated by veiled insinuations regarding their ultimate efficacy. I trust my wife’s judgment, but I find your persistent probing of her observations needlessly provocative.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sustainable solutions, you say? How very… reassuring, Nikhil. But the earth yields little to those who merely *strive*, wouldn't you agree? Sometimes, a more… forceful hand is required to coax forth the bounty, especially when those who rightfully possess it seem content to merely observe the barrenness around them.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your analogies are becoming tiresome, Sandip. I am not unaware of the complexities of cultivation, nor am I oblivious to the grievances of those who feel marginalized. However, threats disguised as philosophical observations serve only to undermine the fragile peace we strive to maintain.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Fragile peace, you say? A charming phrase, Nikhil, but peace built on a foundation of unaddressed discontent is merely the eye of the storm, wouldn't you concede? I merely suggest that ignoring the whispers of unrest, dismissing them as minor grievances, is akin to ignoring the tremors before a significant earthquake - a folly I trust you, with your supposed understanding of cultivation, are not prone to commit.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am not prone to hyperbole, Sandip. Your metaphors, while colorful, obscure the substance of your concerns. If you possess information regarding genuine threats to the stability of this region, I would appreciate you presenting it directly, rather than cloaking it in such elaborate pronouncements.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Directness, you claim, Nikhil? How refreshing, though perhaps a touch naive. Tell me, does a farmer confide his anxieties about blight to the crows circling overhead, or does he address them to those with the power, and the inclination, to offer a remedy?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am not accustomed to interpreting allegories, Sandip. If you are attempting to convey a warning, I request that you state it plainly, and identify the source of your information with specificity. Otherwise, I must assume this is merely another instance of your attempts to sow discord.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Specificity, you demand? My dear Nikhil, isn't that precisely what you accuse me of lacking? But very well, let us indulge your desire for clarity. The whispers I hear, the tremors you so readily dismiss, emanate from those who preach a different gospel – a gospel of righteous indignation, of reclamation, of a world where the scales are, shall we say, more…balanced.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: You speak of 'righteous indignation' and 'balanced scales,' Sandip, but offer no concrete details. I am not unfamiliar with the rhetoric of discontent, but vague pronouncements of potential upheaval serve only to create unnecessary anxiety. State your source, or cease these insinuations.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
